The root cause was that `dashboard/lib/what-now-logic.js` carried its own client-side source vocabulary out of sync with the Python `operator_console._VALID_SOURCES`/`_SOURCE_PRIORITY` (which already admit `upgrade` per D052). I extended the client vocabulary to match: added `'upgrade'` to the frozen `SOURCES` set (so `normalizeActionItem` no longer coerces `source="upgrade"` → `"capability"`), added `upgrade: 'Upgrade'` to `SOURCE_LABELS`, added the four `upgrade:<band>` entries to `VALUE_KIND_LABELS`, and added `upgrade: 6` to `SOURCE_PRIORITY` (mirroring Python's ordering, with slot 5 reserved for `integration` parity) so upgrade items sort with a stable key after architecture. Because normalize now preserves the real source, the `filterItemsForProject` path no longer mis-routes the item through the `capability:` id-prefix branch that was dropping it — it falls through to the unscoped-item keep rule and stays visible in project-scoped views.
